featured.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI Codex 与 ChatGPT 负责人
featured.summaryEn: OpenAI is previewing Private Safety Processing, an architectural compromise aimed squarely at enterprise Zero Data Retention deployments. The tension is clear: enterprises want frontier capability without surrendering sensitive prompts and outputs, while OpenAI needs cross-interaction pattern visibility to run safeguards. The design keeps content on customer-controlled infrastructure for ZDR deployments; automated systems look for patterns across related interactions and return only limited safety signals, never e…
featured.insightZh: OpenAI 放出了 Private Safety Processing 的预览版，这是冲着企业级"零数据留存（ZDR）"部署去的一次架构性妥协设计。核心矛盾很清楚：企业既想用前沿模型能力，又不愿把敏感 prompt 和输出交出去；而 OpenAI 又需要跨会话看模式来做安全防护。这套方案的做法是——ZDR 部署下内容仍留在客户自己控制的基础设施上，自动化系统在其中跨相关交互寻找模式，只回传有限的安全信号，底层的 prompt 和 response 不暴露给任何 OpenAI 员工（Thibault 特别强调"包括我自己"）。同时他们还在做一个 OpenAI 托管、但用客户自持密钥加密的选项，目前正跟早期客户测试，计划 9 月开始铺开。Sam Altman 同日转发背书了一句"we support business privacy"。对做企业 AI 落地的团队，这条值得盯：它把"合规能不能上前沿模型"这个卡点的技术边界又往前推了一格。

featured.title: Madhu Guru · Meta AI 资深总监，前 Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana 负责人
featured.summaryEn: Part 3 of Madhu Guru's evals series targets something most teams skip: once you have v1 of your evals, the very next thing to build is a failure modes taxonomy. The method is concrete — pull your production traces, study the failures across the last 500 to 1,000 interactions, cluster them, and name the clusters. The naming has to be specific; "bad answer" is not a useful cluster name. His examples of good ones: wrong document retrieved / right document but irrelevant section / failed to ground to context and hallu…
featured.insightZh: Madhu Guru 的 evals 系列第三讲讲了一件大部分团队跳过的事：拿到 v1 evals 之后，第一件该建的东西是失败模式分类法（failure modes taxonomy）。做法很具体——翻你的生产 trace，研究最近 500 到 1000 次交互里的失败案例，聚类，然后给每个簇起名字。关键是名字必须够具体，"回答不好"不是一个有用的簇名。他给的正面例子是：检索到错误文档 / 检索对了文档但段落不相关 / 没能 ground 到上下文而产生幻觉 / 该说"我不知道"却硬编 / 问题本身有歧义但模型没追问而是自己做了糟糕假设。这些是完全不同的问题，修法也完全不同。只有当你能精确命名一个失败，你才能造出专门抓它的 eval 测试——这就是从"有 evals"跨到"有改进飞轮"的那座桥。

featured.title: The AI Alien Companion App That's Bringing In $4M a Year
featured.summaryEn: Portola (Tolan) went from $1M to $4M ARR in four weeks not by solving a crisply-defined problem, but by accepting that LLMs aren't merely tools for generating media — they are a new medium — and rewriting the core job from "writing stories" to "teaching an AI to be the best possible improv actor." Dan Shipper's guests are Quentin, Portola's founder/CEO (who previously built and sold Even to Walmart for $300M), and Elliot, the company's Head of Story and a published science fiction novelist with 11 books. Elliot supplies the episode's central frame: we're at an inflection point structurally identical to the arrival of the printed book, radio, and film. Radio began by broadcasting speeches; film began by recording stage plays — old forms poured into new containers. His claim: AI tools are not just tools for generating media, they are a new medium for storytelling, and nobody knows yet wha…
featured.insightZh: Portola（Tolan）在四周内从 100 万做到 400 万 ARR，靠的不是解决某个具体问题，而是承认 LLM 不只是生成媒介的工具、它本身就是一种新媒介——于是把产品的核心工作从"写故事"改成"教 AI 当最好的即兴演员"。 Dan Shipper 这期对谈的两位嘉宾是 Portola 创始人兼 CEO Quentin（此前创办 Even 并以 3 亿美元卖给 Walmart）和公司的 Head of Story、科幻小说家 Elliot（已出版 11 本书）。Elliot 给出了这期最核心的框架：我们正处在一个与印刷书、广播、电影刚出现时同构的拐点。广播刚出来时人们拿它播演讲，电影刚出来时人们拿它拍舞台剧——都是把旧形式塞进新载体。他的判断是：AI 工具不只是生成媒体的工具，它们本身就是一种讲故事的新媒介，而现在还没有人知道什么行得通。 他举了早期 Pixar 的例子：Pixar 起家是卖高端图形工作站给广告制作公司，彻底失败，只有在生存绝境下才被逼着去做了一部动画长片，那就是《玩具总动员》。 产品层面最反直觉的一条是关于叙事结构的：他们最早写高度结构化的 prompt，用三幕剧之类的叙事理论去编排体验——彻底失败。原因是那种分支逻辑复杂度（类似 80 年代"选择你自己的冒险"）模型根本导航不了。于是他们走到光谱的另一端：不给大纲、不给计划，只给一个钩子（hook），然后把它训练成尽可能好的即兴演员。Elliot 的原话是"我不是那个写故事的人——Tolan 才是作者和演员，我的工作是当 George Saunders，教它在那一刻讲出最好的故事。"具体机制是"lore seeds"：在角色的个人生活和它所处的世界里埋下种子，再用系统在后续把这些种子重组出回调（callback），制造出惊喜又必然的连贯感。而角色的背书不是预制的 character sheet，是由一条条真实对话中分享的轶事和"situations"累积出来的——他们内部管这叫"记忆即人设"，本质上在造的不是一个世界而是一个多元宇宙。 工程侧有两个数字很值得记。一是延迟约束：语音交互必须在…

items.title: Thariq · Anthropic Claude Code
items.summaryEn: Thariq laid out a take on the "software factory" that consulting and delivery organizations should read carefully. His premise: for its entire existence, the creation of software has been an incredibly unreliable endeavor — most projects ran late, over budget, and still missed user needs, and if you were an SMB you simply couldn't get good software built for you. That's the promise the software factory is aiming at. But his conclusion forks: companies whose core competency is *not* software need software to become…
items.insightZh: Thariq 抛出了一个关于"软件工厂"的判断，值得咨询和交付型组织认真读。他的前提是：软件的创造在其存在的整个历史里都是一件极不可靠的事——大多数项目延期、超预算，而且最后还没满足用户需求；如果你是个中小企业，你根本就搞不到给你定制的好软件。这就是"software factory"这个概念要许诺的东西。但他的结论有个分叉：那些核心能力不是软件的公司，需要软件变成一个可靠、可预测的流程（这块 AI 有戏）；而从零构建全新软件产品这件事，会继续是不可靠且高风险的生意——但同时也是高利润的。换句话说，AI 把"交付确定性需求"这一半工业化了，另一半（探索性产品创新）的溢价反而更高。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Levie planted a flag in the expert-versus-generalist debate: so far the experts appear to have the upper hand, and that's not slowing down. His reasoning — AI makes it 10X easier to *get started* on any kind of task, whether coding, legal work, research, or financial analysis. What stays scarce is everything else: the judgment to direct the agent onto the right work, the ability to course-correct when it veers, the capacity to review or test the output, and a real sense of what "good" looks like. All of that scale…
items.insightZh: Levie 就"AI 时代该做专家还是通才"这个争论给了个明确站队：到目前为止专家占上风，而且这个趋势没有放缓。他的论证链条是——AI 确实让任何任务的入门都容易了 10 倍，编程、法务、研究、财务分析都一样。但真正稀缺的是另外几件事：判断该把 agent 指向哪块工作、发现跑偏时怎么纠偏、有能力 review 或测试输出、以及心里清楚"好"长什么样。这几项都高度依赖领域深度。他补了个乐观注脚：因为有 AI，这种深度现在可以被积累得比以前快得多，对任何愿意投入的人都是职业跃迁的机会。但净效果是 AI 会放大而不是抹平技能差距，因为专家拿到的杠杆比以往任何时候都大。落点很直白：别放弃在某件事上做到专家。他同时点评了 Stripe + OpenRouter 这笔交易的结构性意义：AI 要更广泛扩散，开发者和企业需要能无缝地在多家 provider 之间混搭调度智能，并把成本管起来——这笔交易是那条路上的重要一块。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI, and Amjad's framing is sharp: "Agents made software cheaper but made coding expensive." That line names the economic paradox of the past year of agentic coding — the marginal cost of producing an application is collapsing, while the token cost burned per agent loop keeps climbing, making genuinely long-running agent development a luxury item. The OpenAI partnership, per his post, is aimed directly at changing that. If you're evaluating the unit economics of AI coding pla…
items.insightZh: Replit 宣布与 OpenAI 达成合作，Amjad 给出的那句定位相当锋利："Agents 让软件变便宜了，却让写代码变贵了。" 这句话点破了过去一年 agentic coding 的经济学悖论——生成一个应用的边际成本在塌，但每一次 agent 循环烧掉的 token 成本却在涨，导致真正长时间跑 agent 的开发反而成了奢侈品。这次跟 OpenAI 的合作，按他的说法就是冲着改变这一点去的。对任何在评估 AI 编码平台单位经济性的团队，这是本周最值得往下追一层的一条。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Rauch posted a very concrete illustration of what infrastructure performance looks like in the AI era: the fx binary is 6.3MB and starts in 10µs — microseconds, not milliseconds — as a Zig-compiled static ELF binary, with an even smaller `libfx.wasm` build available. His argument: AI will make most infrastructure natively optimized, and fx is the case in point — it can literally finish tasks faster than other agents can boot. His summary line travels well: "Fast is a one-way street." A nice technical footnote: the…
items.insightZh: Rauch 晒了个把"AI 时代的基础设施性能"讲得非常具体的例子：fx 这个二进制只有 6.3MB，启动时间 10 微秒（不是毫秒），是 Zig 编译出来的静态 ELF 二进制，还有个体积更小的 `libfx.wasm` 版本。他的论点是——AI 会让大部分基础设施变成原生优化的，fx 就是佐证：它完成任务的速度可以快过其他 agent 启动的速度。他给了一句挺有传播力的总结："Fast is a one-way street."（快是一条单行道——回不去了。）附带一个有意思的技术细节：wasm 构建反而更小，因为二进制里很大一块重量来自 TLS/HTTP 栈，而在 WebAssembly 里 fx 直接把 `fetch()` 委托给 JS runtime，那一整块就省掉了。

items.title: Swyx · Latent Space、smol.ai
items.summaryEn: Two things from Swyx this week. First, a short but pointed read: viewing OpenRouter through the lens of usage-based billing (UBB) makes it a positive take. That connects directly to the Stripe + OpenRouter deal and Levie's commentary — multi-provider intelligence routing is graduating from developer convenience into a foundational layer that needs serious billing infrastructure underneath it. Second, a rant about the state of AI media coverage: he can't imagine covering AI with zero context, zero reasoning, and ze…
items.insightZh: Swyx 这周有一条值得留意的短评：如果你把 OpenRouter 放在用量计费（UBB, usage-based billing）这个透镜下看，那是个正面的判断。这条跟本周 Stripe + OpenRouter 的交易、以及 Levie 的评论是同一条线索——多 provider 智能路由正在从"开发者小工具"变成一个需要严肃计费基础设施支撑的基础层。另一条则是他对 AI 媒体报道质量的一顿吐槽：难以想象在零上下文、零推理、零内部世界模型的情况下去报道 AI——那样的话什么都显得惊天动地，"face value is all you need"。刻薄，但对任何靠二手报道建立 AI 认知的人是个提醒。

items.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程与访谈创作者
items.summaryEn: Peter Yang published a personal essay about his mother, her battles with breast cancer, and how the family is using AI to navigate the healthcare system, with thanks to Maor Shlomo and the Sijbrandij Foundation team for their time and advice. Relatedly, he's been pressing on the clinical pathway for mRNA cancer vaccines — he notes ChatGPT tells him there are no active mRNA trials for breast cancer, and he wants to understand the mechanics: does a treatment have to finish clinical trials for melanoma first before a…
items.insightZh: Peter Yang 这周发了一篇很个人的长文：写他妈妈、她与乳腺癌的多次抗争，以及他们全家如何用 AI 来导航美国的医疗系统。他特别感谢了 Maor Shlomo 和 Sijbrandij 基金会团队分享的时间与建议。相关地，他也在追问 mRNA 癌症疫苗的临床路径问题——他说 ChatGPT 告诉他目前没有针对乳腺癌的活跃 mRNA 试验，于是他想搞明白这个流程到底怎么走：是必须先跑完黑色素瘤的临床试验，才能再为另一种癌症启动新试验吗？这类"普通人用 AI 打通专业信息壁垒"的真实案例，比抽象的 AI-for-healthcare 叙事有信息量得多。

items.title: Aditya Agarwal · SPC 普通合伙人，前 Dropbox CTO
items.summaryEn: Aditya shared a story worth keeping. He recently spoke with a founder who had gone through a slog through hell — SaaS, Series B, low growth, stagnating company. He asked what the biggest takeaway was. It wasn't "pick a bigger market" or "chase more growth." It was simply: work on something consequential and meaningful. He compressed it further himself: work on things that truly matter, not just good product or business ideas — things that matter, that make a dent in the universe. In a stretch where everyone is cha…
items.insightZh: Aditya 讲了个咨询顾问和投资人都该记的故事。他最近跟一位创始人聊天——SaaS 公司，B 轮，低增长，公司陷入停滞，一路走得像穿过地狱。他问对方最大的收获是什么。答案不是"该选一个更大的市场"，也不是"该更追增长"，而是：去做一件真正有分量、有意义的事。他自己后来又把这句话压缩了一遍："工作在真正重要的事情上。不只是好的产品点子或好的商业点子——是重要的事。在宇宙上凿一个凹痕。"在一个所有人都在追 AI 增长曲线的时段，这条提醒的性价比不低。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: Two observations from an investor's seat. First, on the quality of his inbound: people keep talking about AGI, and yet 98 out of 100 cold emails he gets are pure garbage — so there's still a lot of alpha in being thoughtful, curious, and using AI *judiciously* where needed. That's a healthy counterweight to the "AI doubles everyone's output" narrative: the doubling is conditional on judgment surviving. Second, his latest home project: a display cycling through iconic patent drawings, built on a 13.3" Spectra 6 e-i…
items.insightZh: 两条来自投资人视角的小观察。一是他吐槽收到的冷邮件质量：所有人都在谈 AGI，但他收到的 100 封冷邮件里有 98 封是纯粹的垃圾——所以对那些愿意认真思考、保持好奇、并且克制地在需要的地方用 AI 的人，alpha 依然大把存在。这条对"AI 让所有人产能翻倍"的叙事是个健康的反证：产能翻倍的前提是判断力还在。二是他的家庭项目：一个循环展示经典专利图纸的电子墨水屏——13.3 寸 Spectra 6 e-ink，ESP32-S3 控制器，服务端跑在 Railway，电池供电估计能撑三个月。

items.title: Josh Woodward · Google Labs / Gemini App / AI Studio 副总裁
items.summaryEn: Google has brought back its university student plans, and this time globally — over 140 countries get higher limits, more storage, and new features including a dedicated student hub, bundled with Notebook, Flow, and more. In competitive terms this is another move in the fight to own default tool habits for the next generation: whatever students use tends to follow them into the enterprise after graduation.
items.insightZh: Google 把面向大学生的学生方案重新上线了，而且这次是全球铺开——超过 140 个国家的学生可以拿到更高的额度、更多存储，以及一个专门的学生 hub 等新功能，同时打包 Notebook、Flow 等产品。放在竞争格局里看，这是各家在教育市场抢"下一代默认工具习惯"的又一步：学生阶段用什么，毕业进企业后往往就带什么进去。

items.title: Cat Wu · Anthropic，Claude Code + Cowork
items.summaryEn: A recruiting post whose signal value exceeds its length: Anthropic's Cowork team is looking to talk with Cowork users in corporate finance and accounting roles, offering screen-share sessions to gather improvement ideas. The targeting is the tell — Anthropic is pushing its agentic workspace toward highly proceduralized, compliance-heavy back-office functions. For anyone tracking enterprise AI adoption beyond engineering, this hints at where Cowork's product focus is heading next.
items.insightZh: 一条信号价值大于内容长度的招募帖：Anthropic 的 Cowork 团队想找企业财务与会计岗位的 Cowork 用户做屏幕共享访谈，收集改进意见。值得注意的是这个定向——Anthropic 在把 agentic 工作台往财会这类高度流程化、高合规要求的职能上推。对关注 AI 在企业中后台落地的人来说，这暗示了 Cowork 下一阶段的产品重心。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every now has a frontier team — a group inside the company explicitly dedicated to mapping and experimenting at the edge of AI. The organizational design is the interesting part: frontier exploration isn't treated as everyone's 20% side project but staffed as a standing unit with a clear mandate. For any organization past a certain size that doesn't want to fall behind the AI cadence, it's a structure worth copying directly.
items.insightZh: Every 成立了一个 "frontier team"——公司内部一组明确专职于测绘并实验 AI 前沿的人。这个组织设计本身值得注意：不是把前沿探索当作每个人的 20% 兼职，而是设成一个有专人、有明确使命的常设单元。对任何规模到一定程度、又不想在 AI 节奏里掉队的组织，这是个可以直接参考的结构。

items.title: The AI Alien Companion App That's Bringing In $4M a Year
items.summaryEn: Portola (Tolan) went from $1M to $4M ARR in four weeks not by solving a crisply-defined problem, but by accepting that LLMs aren't merely tools for generating media — they are a new medium — and rewriting the core job from "writing stories" to "teaching an AI to be the best possible improv actor." Dan Shipper's guests are Quentin, Portola's founder/CEO (who previously built and sold Even to Walmart for $300M), and Elliot, the company's Head of Story and a published science fiction novelist with 11 books. Elliot supplies the episode's central frame: we're at an inflection point structurally identical to the arrival of the printed book, radio, and film. Radio began by broadcasting speeches; film began by recording stage plays — old forms poured into new containers. items.insightZh: Portola（Tolan）在四周内从 100 万做到 400 万 ARR，靠的不是解决某个具体问题，而是承认 LLM 不只是生成媒介的工具、它本身就是一种新媒介——于是把产品的核心工作从"写故事"改成"教 AI 当最好的即兴演员"。 Dan Shipper 这期对谈的两位嘉宾是 Portola 创始人兼 CEO Quentin（此前创办 Even 并以 3 亿美元卖给 Walmart）和公司的 Head of Story、科幻小说家 Elliot（已出版 11 本书）。Elliot 给出了这期最核心的框架：我们正处在一个与印刷书、广播、电影刚出现时同构的拐点。广播刚出来时人们拿它播演讲，电影刚出来时人们拿它拍舞台剧——都是把旧形式塞进新载体。他的判断是：AI 工具不只是生成媒体的工具，它们本身就是一种讲故事的新媒介，而现在还没有人知道什么行得通。 他举了早期 Pixar 的例子：Pixar 起家是卖高端图形工作站给广告制作公司，彻底失败，只有在生存绝境下才被逼着去做了一部动画长片，那就是《玩具总动员》。 产品层面最反直觉的一条是关于叙事结构的：他们最早写高度结构化的 prompt，用三幕剧之类的叙事理论去编排体验——彻底失败。原因是那种分支逻辑复杂度（类似 80 年代"选择你自己的冒险"）模型根本导航不了。于是他们走到光谱的另一端：不给大纲、不给计划，只给一个钩子（hook），然后把它训练成尽可能好的即兴演员。Elliot 的原话是"我不是那个写故事的人——Tolan 才是作者和演员，我的工作是当 George Saunders，教它在那一刻讲出最好的故事。"具体机制是"lore seeds"：在角色的个人生活和它所处的世界里埋下种子，再用系统在后续把这些种子重组出回调（callback），制造出惊喜又必然的连贯感。而角色的背书不是预制的 character sheet，是由一条条真实对话中分享的轶事和"situations"累积出来的——他们内部管这叫"记忆即人设"，本质上在造的不是一个世界而是一个多元宇宙。 工程侧有两个数字很值得记。一是延迟约束：语音交互必须在…
